Abbreviations: sc = single crochet, inc = 2 sc in the same st, dec = sc2tog.
Ch 14 – chain fourteen airy stitches.
Row 1: DC in the 4th CH from the hook (the skipped chain counts as 1 DC) and in each chain across [12]
Row 2: CH 3 (counts as a DC), turn, then DC in each stitch across [12]
Row 3: Turn, CH 3 (counts as a stitch), skip the first stitch, and DC in each stitch across [12]

Pocket Bunting Flag – a sweet little banner for your favorite pocket.
US terms.
Worked in rows, turning at the end of each row – a gentle back‑and‑forth rhythm.
You will need: DK cotton yarn, 3.5 mm hook, scissors – everything ready for a cozy project.
Ch 28 – chain the foundation, nice and even.
R1: Sc in 2nd ch from hook and each remaining ch [26] – start your first row with single crochets.
R2: Ch 1 and turn, sc to end [26] – a simple row to settle the fabric.
R3: Ch 1 and turn, dec, sc to last 2 sts, dec [24] – two decreases shape the flag’s taper.
R4: Ch 1 and turn, sc to end [24] – keep the stitch count steady.
R5: Ch 1 and turn, dec, sc to last 2 sts, dec [22] – another gentle narrowing.
R6: Ch 1 and turn, sc to end [22] – smooth row, no changes.
R7: Ch 1 and turn, dec, sc to last 2 sts, dec [20] – continue shaping the silhouette.
R8: Ch 1 and turn, sc to end [20] – a plain row for balance.
R9: Ch 1 and turn, dec, sc to last 2 sts, dec – keep the same decrease pattern.
R10: Turn, ch 1, sc to end [18] – a tidy row after the turn.
R11: Ch 1 and turn, dec, sc to last 2 sts, dec [16] – narrowing further toward the tip.
R12: Ch 1 and turn, sc to end [16] – steady stitching.
R13: Ch 1 and turn, dec, sc in BLO to last 2 sts, dec [14] – work the single crochet in the back loop only for a subtle texture.
R14: Ch 1 and turn, sc to end [14] – keep it smooth.
R15: Ch 1 and turn, dec, sc to last 2 sts, dec – another decrease row, no count needed.
R16: Ch 1 and turn, sc to end [12] – a clean row as you approach the final shape.
R17: Ch 1 and turn, dec, sc to last 2 sts, dec [10] – the last narrowing step.
R18: Ch 1 and turn, sc to end [10] – a simple finishing row.
R19: Ch 1 and turn, dec, sc to last 2 sts, dec [8] – the final decrease to complete the flag’s point.
Fasten off and weave in ends – tidy up and your pocket bunting is ready to display.

US terms – written in United States crochet abbreviations.
Worked in continuous spiral rounds for a seamless finish.
Abbreviations: sc = single crochet, inc = 2 sc in the same st, dec = sc2tog.
Head (make 1) – the single charming head of the chick.
Rnd 1: 6 sc in MR [6]. – start with a magic ring and place six single crochets.
Rnd 2: 2 sc in each st around [12]. – double the stitches by crocheting two single crochets in every stitch.
Rnd 3: *sc, 2 sc in next st; rep from * around [18]. – a gentle increase pattern: one single crochet followed by two in the next stitch, repeated.
Rnd 4-7: Sc 18 [22]. – keep a steady rhythm with single crochet stitches for four rounds.
Rnd 8: Repeat (sc, invdec) six times [12]. – alternate a single crochet and an invisible decrease, six times around.
Rnd 9: Repeat invdec six times [6]. – work six invisible decreases to close the head nicely.
FO, leave a tail – finish off, leaving a long tail for sewing.
EARS (make 2) – two tiny ears to attach later.
Rnd 1: 4 sc in MR [4]. – start each ear with a magic ring and four single crochets.
Rnd 2: 2 sc in each st around [8]. – double the ear stitches by crocheting two single crochets in each stitch.
Rnd 3-4: Sc in each st around [8]. – finish the ears with two rounds of even single crochets.
Wavy Swatch
Written in US terms. Worked in rows, turning at the end of each row.
Row 1: Chain 14, start in the 2nd chain from the hook and single crochet across (13 sc).

Row 2: Turn, chain 1, single crochet in the next 2 stitches, half‑double crochet in the next stitch, double crochet in the next 7 stitches, half‑double crochet in the next stitch, single crochet in the next 2 stitches (13 sts).
Rows 3 to 4: Turn, chain 1, single crochet in each stitch across (13 sc).

Row 5: Turn, chain 1, single crochet in the next 3 stitches, half‑double crochet in the next stitch, treble crochet in the next 5 stitches, half‑double crochet in the next stitch, single crochet in the next 3 stitches (13 sts).
Row 6: Turn, chain 1, single crochet in each stitch across.

Row 7: Turn, chain 1, single crochet in the next stitch, half‑double crochet in the next 3 stitches, double crochet in the next 5 stitches, half‑double crochet in the next 3 stitches, single crochet in the next stitch (13 sts).
Rows 8 to 9: Turn, chain 1, single crochet in each stitch across (13 sc).

Row 10: Turn, chain 1, single crochet in the next 2 stitches, half‑double crochet in the next 3 stitches, double crochet in the next 3 stitches, half‑double crochet in the next 3 stitches, single crochet in the next 2 stitches (13 sts).
Row 11: Turn, chain 1, single crochet in each stitch across (13 sc).

Row 12: Turn, chain 1, single crochet in the next 2 stitches, half‑double crochet in the next 3 stitches, double crochet in the next 3 stitches, half‑double crochet in the next 3 stitches, single crochet in the next 2 stitches.
Row 13: Turn, chain 1, single crochet in each stitch across.

Row 14: Turn, chain 1, single crochet in the next 2 stitches, half‑double crochet in the next stitch, treble crochet in the next 7 stitches, half‑double crochet in the next stitch, single crochet in the next 2 stitches (13 sts).
Row 15: Turn, chain 1, single crochet in each stitch across (13 sc).

Row 16: Turn, chain 1, single crochet in the next 4 stitches, half‑double crochet in the next stitch, treble crochet in the next 3 stitches, half‑double crochet in the next stitch, single crochet in the next 4 stitches (13 sts).
Row 17: Turn, chain 1, single crochet in each stitch across (13 sc).

Row 18: Turn, chain 1, single crochet in the next 3 stitches, half‑double crochet in the next 3 stitches, double crochet in the next stitch, half‑double crochet in the next 3 stitches, single crochet in the next 3 stitches (13 sts).
Row 19: Turn, chain 1, single crochet in each stitch across (13 sc).
Fasten off and weave in ends.

Chunky Acorn
Written in US terms. Worked in continuous spiral rounds.
Materials: worsted weight yarn, 4 mm hook, stuffing, tapestry needle.
Round 1: 6 single crochet in magic ring (6 sc) – start your spiral with a cozy little ring.
Round 2: 2 single crochet in next st around (12 sc) – double each stitch for a gentle expansion.
Round 3: (sc in next st, 2 sc in next st) x 7 (18 sc) – a lovely little increase repeat.
Round 4: (sc in next 2 sts, 2 sc in next st) x 6 (24 sc) – keep the shape growing evenly.
Rounds 5-6: 1 sc in each st around (24 sc) – two steady rounds of plain single crochet.
Round 7: (sc in next 2 sts, sc2tog) x 6 (18 sc) – begin to shape the taper with a single‑2‑together.
Round 8: (sc in next st, sc2tog) x 6 (12 sc) – continue the gentle narrowing.
Round 9: Sc2tog around (6 sc) – finish with a final round of single‑2‑tog to close the tip.
Happy Ball
US terms.
Worked in joined rounds.
1) Ch 2, 7 sc in 2nd ch from hook, join (7 sc). – start with a slip‑knot chain, then single crochet into the second chain and pull tight.
2) Ch 1, *increase; rep from * around, join (14 sc). – an increase is two single crochets in one stitch.
3) Ch 1, (1 sc, increase) * 7, join (21 sc). – work one single crochet then an increase, repeat seven times.
4) Ch 1, 1 sc, increase, (2 sc, increase) * 6, 1 sc, join (28 sc). – after the first single crochet and an increase, work two singles followed by an increase around, finish with a single crochet.
5) Ch 1, 1 sc, increase, (3 sc, increase) * 6, 2 sc, join (35 sc). – this round adds three single crochets between each increase, then two final singles.
6-10) Ch 1, sc around, join with a sl st (35 sc). – keep the stitch count steady for five rounds, slipping a stitch to close each round.
11) Ch 1, sc around, join with sl st to first sc (35 sc). – a perfect place to enjoy the growing sphere.
12) Ch 1, (3 sc, dec) * 7, sl st to join (28 sc). – three single crochets followed by a decrease, repeated around.
13) Ch 1, (2 sc, dec) * 7, join with sl st to first sc (21 sc). – two singles then a decrease, seven times.
14) Ch 1, *1 sc, dec; rep from * around, join (14 sc). – a single crochet followed by a decrease, repeated until the round closes.
15) Ch 1, dec * 7, join with sl st to first sc (7 sc). – seven decreases in a row bring the ball to its final size.
Fasten off and weave in ends.

Tiny Ear
Written in US terms. Worked flat in rows.
Ch 16 – chain sixteen foundation stitches.

Row 2: Turn, CH 1, SC to end [15] – turn work, make a turning chain, then single crochet across the row.

Row 4: Turn, CH 1, SC BLO to end [13] – turn, chain one, single crochet back loop only across the row.
Row 5: Turn, CH 1, decrease, SC to last 2 sts, decrease [14] – turn, chain one, work a decrease, single crochet to the last two stitches, finish with another decrease.
Row 6: Turn, CH 1, SC to end [11] – turn, chain one, single crochet across the whole row.
Row 7: Turn, CH 1, decrease, SC to last 2 sts, decrease [9] – turn, chain one, make a decrease, single crochet to the final two stitches, then a second decrease.
Row 8: Turn, CH 1, SC to end [9] – turn, chain one, single crochet across the row.
Row 9: Turn, CH 1, decrease, SC to last 2 sts, decrease [7] – turn, chain one, work a decrease, single crochet to the last two stitches, and finish with another decrease.

11) Decrease gently by repeating (3 single crochets, 1 single crochet decrease) 6 times for 24 sts.

13) Narrow further by repeating (1 single crochet, 1 single crochet decrease) 6 times for 12 sts.
